@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# Plan: Make PR #7 and PR #8 CI green
+
+Both PRs in alehar9320/agentic-odi have failing CI. Fix root causes with real
+fixes (tests first), verify locally mirroring CI, push, watch checks.
+
+Global constraints:
+- Never weaken security scanning to get green (no bandit config skips).
+- Mirror CI commands exactly for local verification.
+- Work only in the two existing worktrees:
+  - PR #8: .worktrees/cli-bundled-distribution (feature/cli-bundled-distribution)
+  - PR #7: .worktrees/living-studio-tauri (topic/living-studio-tauri)
+- No rebase needed (both MERGEABLE on current origin/main).
+
+## Root causes (evidence verified)
+
+### PR #8 — security job (then CI green; smoke skipped, never ran)
+Bandit, 6 issues in cli/src:
+1. B110 (low) cli/src/cli/cli.py:42-43 — `except Exception: pass` in `_startup_auto_update`
+2. B606 (low) cli/src/cli/cli.py:78 — `os.execv` re-exec of own binary
+3. B202 (med) cli/src/cli/update.py:79 — `zf.extractall(dest)` (bandit flags any
+   `extractall` when the module also imports `tarfile`; CPython `_extract_member`
+   strips `..`/absolute paths — verified in stdlib source)
+4. B202 (med) cli/src/cli/update.py:82 — `tf.extractall(dest)` unvalidated
+5. B310 (high) cli/src/cli/update.py:168 — `urlopen` (`# noqa: S310` affects neither ruff nor bandit)
+6. B310 (high) cli/src/cli/update.py:173 — same
+All other scanned srcs clean. Bandit accepts literal `filter="data"` kwarg
+(verified in bandit 1.9.4 plugin source: returns None → no issue).
+All URLs derive from https constants (RELEASES_API, _RELEASES_DOWNLOAD).
+
+### PR #7 — studio + tauri-build + smoke (then CI green)
+1. TS2307 `Cannot find module '../../lib/odi'` — `studio/src/lib/{odi.ts,odi.test.ts}`
+   exist on disk but were never committed: root `.gitignore` unanchored `lib/`
+   (stock Python template) swallows any dir named lib. Verified: root `lib/` never
+   existed in history, no script writes it, all Python pkgs use src/ layout,
+   venv libs covered by `.venv/`/`venv/`/`env/`.
+2. Smoke sidecar probe 422s: POST `/api/health/mcp` with `{}` but
+   `McpHealthRequest.mcp_url` is required; GET `/api/canvas` missing required
+   `mcp_url` query. Both curl legs fail (verified in run log + router.py + tests).
+3. Steps never reached after early failures: studio unit tests/build/gen-check,
+   client.run smoke step — must de-risk locally.
+Decision (user-approved evaluation): anchor `lib/` → `/lib/`, `lib64/` → `/lib64/`;
+keep the canonical `studio/src/lib` name (industry-standard TS source dir).
+
+## Task 1: PR #8 — failing tests first
+- Worktree cli-bundled-distribution. In cli/tests/test_update.py add:
+  - `test_extract_archive_rejects_tar_path_traversal`: tar with member
+    `../escape.txt` → `extract_archive` must raise and no file may appear outside dest.
+    RED now (extractall without filter writes outside).
+  - `test_extract_archive_contains_zip_path_traversal`: zip member `../evil.txt`
+    → extracted only under dest, no escape (documents zipfile sanitization).
+  - `test_default_fetch_rejects_non_https`: `update._default_fetch("file:///<tmp>")`
+    → raises `update.UpdateError` and does not return file content. RED now.
+Expected: pytest shows the two RED tests failing for the right reasons.
+
+## Task 2: PR #8 — real fixes
+- update.py `extract_archive`: tar branch → `tf.extractall(dest, filter="data")`;
+  zip branch → keep + `# nosec B202 - ZipFile._extract_member strips absolute/'..' paths`.
+- update.py: add `_require_https(url)` (raise `UpdateError` unless scheme == "https"),
+  call from `_default_fetch` and `_default_fetch_bytes`; replace `# noqa: S310` with
+  `# nosec B310 - scheme enforced by _require_https`.
+- cli.py: `pass` → `return None` (keep `# noqa: BLE001`).
+- cli.py:78: trailing `# nosec B606` + justification (re-execs own verified binary).
+Expected: new tests GREEN; full cli suite GREEN.
+
+## Task 3: PR #8 — local CI mirror + smoke de-risk
+- `uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src connectors/src` → exit 0
+- `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` → clean
+- mypy: `uv run --directory <pkg> mypy .` for core, mcp_server, local_server, cli, client, connectors
+- `uv run --directory cli pytest` → all pass
+- Smoke steps (never ran on this PR): `uv run python -m cli --version`;
+  `uv run python -m cli connectors --help` greps for list+ingest;
+  MCP server boot probe on :8000 (verbatim from ci.yml); client.run probe (verbatim).
+
+## Task 4: PR #8 — commit + push + watch
+- Commit with repo-style message; push; `gh pr checks 8 --watch`.
+
+## Task 5: PR #7 — gitignore + track src/lib
+- Worktree living-studio-tauri. Root `.gitignore`: `lib/` → `/lib/`, `lib64/` → `/lib64/`.
+- `git add studio/src/lib` (odi.ts, odi.test.ts); confirm nothing else newly unignored
+  (`git status --short` shows only intended files).
+
+## Task 6: PR #7 — fix smoke probe 422s
+- ci.yml sidecar probe:
+  - `-d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}'`
+  - `http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/canvas?mcp_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`
+- Expected: both legs 200 (health returns reachable=false when MCP down; canvas
+  falls back to seed payload — verified in probes.py/mcp_data.py).
+
+## Task 7: PR #7 — local verification (incl. never-reached steps)
+- `cd studio && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run
+  && npm run build && npm run gen:api-types && git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts`
+- Run edited sidecar probe verbatim (sidecar via `uv run python -m local_server.main`).
+- Run client.run probe verbatim (never ran in CI).
+- tauri-build: frontend `npm run build` is the actual CI failure (covered above);
+  cargo side previously green in tauri-check; full `npm run tauri build` only if
+  system webkit deps available locally.
+
+## Task 8: PR #7 — commit + push + watch
+- Commit; push; `gh pr checks 7 --watch`.
+
+## Task 9: Final review
+- Review both diffs against plan; verification-before-completion before any
+  success claim; report rulings/deferreds.

## Locked decisions
- **Standard:** Conventional Commits + Conventional Branch names + semver tags `vX.Y.Z`.
- **Prose:** fully automated AI rewrite, each release carries an AI disclaimer, with grounding guardrails.
- **Runtime delivery:** CLI/GUI fetches `changelog.json` from GitHub Releases.
- **Not a source file:** nothing generated is committed; no `CHANGELOG.md`, so no merge conflicts.

## Design

**1. The standard (repo convention, enforced)**
- Commit: `type(scope): subject`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Scopes = packages (`cli`, `client`, `connectors`, `core`, `mcp_server`, `local_server`) plus `ci`, `deps`, `release`, `workspace`. Breaking change = `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- Branch: `feature/`, `fix/`, `hotfix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `release/` + `kebab-case`.
- Semver: breaking→major, `feat`→minor, else patch (pre-1.0 breaking may be a builder call to map to minor).
- Enforcement: `commitizen` (`cz check`) as a `commit-msg` pre-commit hook + `cz commit`; CI checks the **PR title** and the **branch name**. This requires **squash-only merges** with conventional PR titles — which also cleans up going forward (your existing history is mixed: bare `Add …`, `Refactor architecture: …`, plus merge commits).

**2. The generator (release-time, AI)**
- Input = a **grounding manifest**: every commit since the last tag (sha, subject, body, PR number, files changed, diffstat). This is the only source material.
- A provider-agnostic script (`scripts/changelog/generate.py`, reusing the OpenAI SDK already in `client`) rewrites entries into user-facing prose grouped as **Added / Improved / Fixed / Removed / Security**, temperature 0, schema-constrained JSON.
- **Guardrails:** every entry must cite ≥1 source sha; any sha not in the manifest is rejected; entries with no source are rejected; a coverage check flags user-visible commits that vanished; a grounding heuristic flags proper-nouns/idents not present in source; the run fails closed. Output is a draft the maintainer approves before publish.

**3. Storage/delivery**
- A tag-triggered workflow writes the result to the GitHub Release body and uploads `changelog.json` (schema-validated) as a release asset. Each release carries the AI disclaimer (in prose and a `generated_by: "ai"` field).

**4. Runtime ("since the version you last ran")**
- `changelog.json` embeds `{version, date, sections[], sources[], generated_by}`.
- Shared pure model/render + stdlib fetch live in **`core`** (so CLI *and* the Streamlit GUI reuse them). CLI exposes `odi whats-new` / `odi changelog [--since X.Y.Z] [--all] [--json]`. The distribution plan's state file gains `last_run_version`; the command shows entries between that and the installed version, then updates state.

**5. Backfill**
- Pre-`0.1.0` messy history is summarized by the same AI process into a single grounded **"Initial release (0.1.0)"** entry.

- **Standard:** Conventional Commits + Conventional Branch names + semver tags `vX.Y.Z`.

## Design

**1. The standard (repo convention, enforced)**
- Commit: `type(scope): subject`. Types: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Scopes = packages (`cli`, `client`, `connectors`, `core`, `mcp_server`, `local_server`) plus `ci`, `deps`, `release`, `workspace`. Breaking change = `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- Branch: `feature/`, `fix/`, `hotfix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`, `refactor/`, `test/`, `release/` + `kebab-case`.
- Semver: breaking→major, `feat`→minor, else patch (pre-1.0 breaking may be a builder call to map to minor).
- Enforcement: `commitizen` (`cz check`) as a `commit-msg` pre-commit hook + `cz commit`; CI checks the **PR title** and the **branch name**. This requires **squash-only merges** with conventional PR titles — which also cleans up going forward (your existing history is mixed: bare `Add …`, `Refactor architecture: …`, plus merge commits).

**2. The generator (release-time, AI)**
- Input = a **grounding manifest**: every commit since the last tag (sha, subject, body, PR number, files changed, diffstat). This is the only source material.
- A provider-agnostic script (`scripts/changelog/generate.py`, reusing the OpenAI SDK already in `client`) rewrites entries into user-facing prose grouped as **Added / Improved / Fixed / Removed / Security**, temperature 0, schema-constrained JSON.
- **Guardrails:** every entry must cite ≥1 source sha; any sha not in the manifest is rejected; entries with no source are rejected; a coverage check flags user-visible commits that vanished; a grounding heuristic flags proper-nouns/idents not present in source; the run fails closed. Output is a draft the maintainer approves before publish.

**3. Storage/delivery**
- A tag-triggered workflow writes the result to the GitHub Release body and uploads `changelog.json` (schema-validated) as a release asset. Each release carries the AI disclaimer (in prose and a `generated_by: "ai"` field).

**4. Runtime ("since the version you last ran")**
- `changelog.json` embeds `{version, date, sections[], sources[], generated_by}`.
- Shared pure model/render + stdlib fetch live in **`core`** (so CLI *and* the Streamlit GUI reuse them). CLI exposes `odi whats-new` / `odi changelog [--since X.Y.Z] [--all] [--json]`. The distribution plan's state file gains `last_run_version`; the command shows entries between that and the installed version, then updates state.

**5. Backfill**
- Pre-`0.1.0` messy history is summarized by the same AI process into a single grounded **"Initial release (0.1.0)"** entry.

# First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** On first interactive launch, the CLI captures a PM baseline via URL auto-detect with typed fallback, persists it to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json`, and exposes `setup`/`profile` commands; the first-run hook never fires again once the file exists.

**Architecture:** Three new modules in the `cli` package: `profile.py` (baseline model, XDG config path, atomic load/save, `setup`/`profile` Typer sub-app), `infer.py` (deterministic keyword-based domain/business-model inference from page text), `onboard.py` (httpx fetch + stdlib HTML signal extraction, confirmation card, typed fallback, first-run hook). The hook is wired into the existing root Typer callback in `cli.py`.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, Typer, httpx (new declared `cli` dependency), stdlib `html.parser`, pytest, uv.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-first-run-onboarding-design.md`

## Global Constraints

- Python `>= 3.10`; CLI package `agentic-odi-cli`, entry `cli.cli:app`.
- Config dir: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/agentic-odi` → `~/.config/agentic-odi` (Windows: `%APPDATA%\agentic-odi`); baseline file `baseline.json`.
- All user-facing copy renders the invoked program name via `Path(sys.argv[0]).name` (helper `cli.cli_name()`), never a hard-coded `odi`/`agentic-odi`.
- No LLM calls, no network in tests (httpx `MockTransport` only), no writes outside the XDG config dir (tests override `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` / `HOME` via monkeypatch + tmp_path).
- Schema: only `schema_version` is required; all other fields may be `null`/empty; confirmation card renders only non-null lines. JSON keys are **flat** (`product_name`, `product_url`) rather than the spec's nested `product` object — simpler for the dataclass round-trip (builder call).
- `--version` needs no guard in the hook: the eager Typer option callback raises `Exit` during parsing, before the root callback body runs.

(Task 3) 2. **Non-interactive first run (CI, pipes)** — one hint line, command continues, never blocks. (Task 5) 3. **Confidently wrong inference** — card always shown; nothing written to disk before the user confirms. (Task 5) 4. **Concurrent first runs** — atomic temp-file + `os.replace` write; no partial `baseline.json`. (Task 1) 5. **`--version` / `--help`** — never trigger onboarding. (Task 5) --- ### Task 1: Baseline model, config path, atomic persistence **Files:** - Create: `cli/src/cli/profile.py` - Test: `cli/tests/test_profile.py` **Interfaces:** - Consumes: nothing. - display.text:
name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: linux_x86_64
            container: quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_x86_64:latest
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: linux_arm64
            container: quay.io/pypa/manylinux2014_aarch64:latest
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-14
            target: macos_arm64
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-13
            target: macos_x86_64
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            target: windows_x86_64
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    container: ${{ matrix.container }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup uv
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          uv-version: "0.8.22"
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Build
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          RELEASE_DATE_UTC: ${{ github.event.repository.pushed_at || github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          RELEASE_DATE_UTC=$(git log -1 --format=%cI)
          export VERSION RELEASE_DATE_UTC
          bash scripts/build_binary.sh
      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for f in odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip; do echo "hash $f"; done
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            sha256sum odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip > checksums.txt 2>/dev/null || true
          elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            shasum -a 256 odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip > checksums.txt 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
        shell: bash
      - name: Upload assets
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            odi_*.tar.gz
            odi_*.zip
            checksums.txt

  upload-installers:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Upload install scripts
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            scripts/install.sh
            scripts/install.ps1

27: def _version_callback(ctx: typer.Context, value: bool) -> None:
28:     if value:
29:         if ctx.params.get("verbose"):
30:             typer.echo(version.verbose_summary())
31:         else:
32:             typer.echo(version.build_summary())
33:         raise typer.Exit()
34: 
35: 
36: def _startup_auto_update(no_update: bool) -> None:
37:     """Best-effort background auto-update; never raises, never blocks."""
38:     try:
39:         updated = update.maybe_auto_update(no_update=no_update, now=time.time())
40:         if updated is not None:
41:             typer.echo(f"Updated to v{updated} — takes effect next run")
42:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
43:         pass
44: 
45: 
46: @app.callback()
47: def main(
48:     version: bool = typer.Option(
49:         False, "--version", callback=_version_callback, help="Show version"
50:     ),
51:     verbose: bool = typer.Option(
52:         False,
53:         "--verbose",
54:         is_eager=True,
55:         help="Show verbose version information (with --version)",
56:     ),
57:     backend: str | None = typer.Option(None, "--backend", help="Backend: local | mcp"),
58:     no_update: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-update", help="Disable the startup update check"),
59: ) -> None:  # noqa: B008
60:     context.set_backend(backend)
61:     if not no_update:
62:         threading.Thread(target=_startup_auto_update, args=(no_update,), daemon=True).start()
63: 
64: 
65: def _reexec_current() -> None:
66:     """Re-exec into the freshly installed binary (POSIX only)."""
67:     current = paths.current_link()
68:     binary = current / "odi"
69:     can_exec = (
70:         os.name == "posix" and hasattr(os, "execv") and current.is_symlink() and binary.exists()
71:     )
72:     if not can_exec:
73:         typer.echo("Update applied; it will take effect on the next run.")
74:         return
75:     argv = sys.argv[1:]
76:     if "update" in argv:
77:         argv = argv[: argv.index("update")]
78:     os.execv(str(binary), [str(binary), *argv])
79: 
80: 
81: @app.command(name="version")
82: def version_cmd() -> None:
83:     """Show CLI version."""
84:     typer.echo(version.build_summary())
85: 
86: 
87: @app.command(name="update")
88: def update_cmd(
89:     check: bool = False,
90:     force: bool = False,
91:     version: str | None = None,
92:     now: bool = False,
93: ) -> None:
94:     """Check for or apply CLI updates."""
95:     if check:
96:         latest = update.latest_release(__version__)
97:         if latest is None:
98:             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
99:         else:
100:             typer.echo(f"Update available: v{latest} - run 'odi update' to install.")
101:         return
102: 
103:     if not paths.is_frozen():
104:         typer.echo("This is a source install; use your package manager to update.")
105:         return
106: 
107:     target = version.lstrip("v") if version else update.latest_release(__version__)
108:     if target is None:
109:         if force:
110:             target = __version__
111:         else:
112:             typer.echo(f"Already up to date (v{__version__}).")
113:             return
114: 
115:     try:
116:         with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="odi-update-") as tmp:
117:             archive = update.download(target, Path(tmp))
118:             digest = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
119:             update.perform_update(target, archive, digest, paths.install_root())
120:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
121:         typer.echo(f"Update failed: {exc}", err=True)
122:         raise typer.Exit(code=1) from exc
123: 
124:     typer.echo(f"Updated to v{target}")
125:     if now:
126:         _reexec_current()
127: 
128: 
129: if __name__ == "__main__":
130:     app()

<content>
1: # First-Run Onboarding (PM Baseline) Design
2: 
3: **Date:** 2026-10-16
4: **Status:** Approved
5: **Scope:** CLI first-launch experience + persistent PM baseline profile
6: 
7: ## Intent & Why
8: 
9: Agentic ODI ships 69 PM skills (vendored from Paweł Huryn's pm-skills) and an ODI/JTBD agent, but nothing establishes *who the user is* — domain, audience, business model, current goal. Every skill run starts cold, asking generic questions or guessing. The fix: one designed first-run moment that captures (mostly auto-detects) a minimal product/domain baseline, persists it, and lets the agent and skills consume it forever after.
10: 
11: Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. They give **one input — a product URL or company name** — the CLI fetches and infers, prints a small confirmation card, and one keypress completes setup. Typed questions exist only as fallback when the fetch fails or inference is unclear. Total happy-path effort: ~30 seconds, one keystroke.
12: 
13: ## Goals
14: 
15: - First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
16: - Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
17: - Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
18: - Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
19: - `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
20: - PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).
21: 
22: ## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals
23: 
24: - No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
25: - No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
26: - No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
27: - No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
28: - No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).
29: 
30: ## User Flow
31: 
32: ### 1. Trigger
33: 
34: - Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
35: - Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
36: - Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.
37: 
38: ### 2. Opening (the designed moment)
39: 
40: ```
41: Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.
42: 
43: Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
44: First: what product are you working on?
45: Paste a product URL or company name:
46: ```
47: 
48: ### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect
49: 
50: 1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
51: 2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
52: 3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
53: 4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
54: 5. Show the confirmation card:
55: 
56: ```
57: Based on sentry.io — does this look right?
58: 
59:   Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
60:   Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
61:   Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
62:   Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging
63: 
64:   [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
65: ```
66: 
67: 6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).
68: 
69: ### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)
70: 
71: Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):
72: 
73: 1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
74: 2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
75: 3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).
76: 
77: Then the same confirmation card and save.
78: 
79: ### 5. After onboarding
80: 
81: - Baseline file presence suppresses the hook forever.
82: - `odi setup` — full re-run, overwrites file (keeps a timestamped backup).
83: - `odi profile` — print the current card from the file. (`setup`/`profile` confirmed: plain language, matches the reserved `odi` alias.)
84: - All user-facing copy (hints, "Try: …" lines) uses the invoked program name (`sys.argv[0]` basename) so it is valid on any install, `odi` or `agentic-odi`.
85: - Skills/agent consumption (future): the file path is stable and documented; `odi profile --json` dumps machine-readable baseline.
86: 
87: ## Data Model
88: 
89: `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (dir per XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Windows %APPDATA%):
90: 
91: ```json
92: {
93:   "schema_version": 1,
94:   "created_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
95:   "source": "url" | "typed",
96:   "product": {"name": "Sentry", "url": "https://sentry.io"},
97:   "domain": "Developer Tools / Observability",
98:   "primary_user": "Software engineers & DevOps teams",
99:   "business_model": "B2B SaaS · Product-led growth",
100:   "core_problem": "Real-time application error tracking & code-level debugging",
101:   "current_focus": null | "launch" | "activation" | "retention" | "scaling" | "discovery",
102:   "confidence": "high" | "low"
103: }
104: ```
105: 
106: Missing/optional fields are `null`, not guessed — later skills ask just-in-time for what they need. The typed path stays at 3 questions; `product.name` may be empty, `business_model`/`core_problem`/`current_focus` may be null, and the confirmation card renders only the lines we actually know.
107: 
108: ## Code Layout (new)
109: 
110: ```
111: cli/src/cli/onboard.py      # flow orchestration (prompt, fetch, confirm, save)
112: cli/src/cli/profile.py      # load/save baseline, `profile` + `setup` commands
113: cli/src/cli/infer.py        # heuristic domain/model inference from page text
114: cli/tests/test_onboard.py
115: cli/tests/test_infer.py
116: cli/tests/test_profile.py
117: ```
118: 
119: - `paths` helper lives in `profile.py` for now (config dir resolution only: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.config`, Windows `%APPDATA%`), deliberately minimal to avoid coupling to the distribution plan.
120: - httpx used for fetch; inference has no network/LLM deps.
121: 
122: ## Copy & Polish Rules (the Jobsian part)
123: 
124: - Total onboarding text on screen at once: one card, no scrolling paragraph.
125: - Voice: warm, direct, second person; no jargon dumps; no emoji.
126: - Every prompt has a sensible default or suggestion; Enter almost always works.
127: - Failure is silent-and-graceful: fetch errors fall to typed path without a scary traceback; one soft line (`Couldn't read that site — two quick questions instead.`).
128: - `--no-onboard` global flag to bypass (for scripting/tests); env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_ONBOARD=1` equivalent.
129: 
130: ## Constraints
131: 
132: - Python 3.10+, Typer, pytest — already in the workspace. `httpx` is **added** as a declared dependency of the `cli` package (builder check correction: it was not one; it is the fetch client of choice, and its `MockTransport` powers the fetch tests). Tests must not touch the real home dir (tmp_path + env overrides).
133: - Fetch tests use mocked transport (`httpx.MockTransport`), never live network.
134: 
135: ## Review Focus (likely to bite)
136: 
137: 1. Fetch hang/timeout on weird sites — hard 8s timeout, errors → typed path.
138: 2. TTY detection wrong in some terminals — conservative check; hint-line behavior in non-TTY.
139: 3. Inference confidently wrong — confirmation card always shown; nothing saved without confirm.
140: 4. Concurrent first runs — file written atomically (temp file + replace).
141: 5. `--version` and help must never trigger onboarding.
142: 
143: ## Resolved Questions
144: 
145: 1. Command naming: **`odi setup` / `odi profile`** (plain language; matches reserved `odi` alias). Copy uses the invoked program name.
146: 2. `current_focus`: **just-in-time only** — not asked on the happy path; asked as the 3rd typed question in the fallback path.
147: 
148: ## Builder Calls (made during review)
149: 
150: 1. Typed-path fields: schema fields other than `schema_version` are nullable; card renders only non-null lines.
151: 2. `httpx` added as an explicit `cli` package dependency (spec previously, incorrectly, claimed it already was).

(End of file - total 151 lines)
</content>

**Status:** Approved

Jobsian bar: the PM should never fill out a form. ## Goals

- First `agentic-odi` invocation (interactive TTY) triggers a short, designed onboarding moment instead of a bare help screen.
- Happy path: **URL → fetch → infer → confirm card → done**.
- Fallback path (fetch fails / non-obvious site / user prefers typing): **3 typed questions with suggested defaults**.
- Baseline persisted to `~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (XDG-overridable); never re-prompts once the file exists.
- `odi setup` re-runs onboarding; `odi profile` shows the current baseline.
- PM skills / agent can later read the baseline file as standing context; follow-ups happen only when a specific task needs missing fields (out of scope to implement here beyond exposing the file and a `profile` command).

## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

- No long diagnostic questionnaire (the 15-question PM audit is explicitly rejected).
- No LLM call during onboarding (no API key exists yet at first run; inference must be deterministic, offline-capable keyword mapping).
- No storage of secrets (API keys stay in env, as today).
- No GUI/Streamlit changes (CLI only; GUI can adopt the file later).
- No dependency on the unfinished bundled-distribution work (`paths.py`, auto-update). If that plan lands first, its `paths.config_dir()` should replace the local helper (see Open Questions).

## User Flow

### 1. Trigger

- Hook in the root Typer callback (`cli/src/cli/cli.py` `main()`).
- Runs only when: baseline file absent **AND** stdin/stdout are TTYs **AND** command is not `--version`/`version` and not `setup`/`profile` (those manage it explicitly).
- Non-interactive first run (pipes, CI): print one hint line — `Run 'odi setup' to create your PM baseline.` — and continue; never block.

### 2. Opening (the designed moment)

```
Agentic ODI — your ODI/JTBD + PM-skills workspace.

Let's set up your context so every skill starts smart.
First: what product are you working on?
Paste a product URL or company name:
```

### 3. Happy path — URL auto-detect

1. Accept URL or bare name (normalize `acme.com` → `https://acme.com`).
2. Fetch with httpx (httpx already a workspace dep): homepage, ~8s timeout, no retries, follow ≤3 redirects, conservative UA header. Optionally try `/pricing` and `/about` if homepage text is thin (<200 words).
3. Extract signals: `<title>`, meta description, og tags, H1/H2 text, nav labels, pricing hints ("per seat", "free tier", "usage-based").
4. **Inference engine** (pure-Python heuristic, `onboard/infer.py`): keyword dictionaries map extracted text → domain archetype (DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, MarTech, Marketplace, B2B SaaS, B2C, etc.), business model hints (PLG/freemium vs sales-led), and candidate primary user. Deterministic and unit-testable; low-confidence results fall back to the typed path with the inferred values pre-filled as suggestions.
5. Show the confirmation card:

```
Based on sentry.io — does this look right?

  Domain      Developer Tools / Observability
  Users       Software engineers, DevOps teams
  Business    B2B SaaS · Product-led (freemium → team plans)
  Solves      Real-time error tracking & debugging

  [Enter] confirm   [e] edit a line   [r] retry URL   [q] quit
```

6. `e` asks only for the lines the user picks, with current value as the default. `r` returns to URL prompt. Confirm writes `baseline.json` and prints a one-line success (`Saved to ~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json — you're set. Try: odi outcomes list`).

### 4. Fallback — typed path (3 questions)

Entered on fetch failure, low inference confidence, or if the user types `skip` at the URL prompt. Each question offers suggestions (from partial inference when available):

1. **Domain** — free text with hint list (B2B SaaS, DevTools, FinTech, HealthTech, Marketplace, …).
2. **Who uses it** — primary user/job ("e.g., Staff engineers reducing CI friction").
3. **What matters most right now** — launch / activation / retention / scaling / discovery (single select from menu via arrow keys — Typer+readchar or plain numbered menu; numbered menu chosen for zero extra deps).

Then the same confirmation card and save.

### 5. After onboarding

## Data Model

`~/.config/agentic-odi/baseline.json` (dir per XDG_CONFIG_HOME, Windows %APPDATA%):

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "created_at": "2026-10-16T12:00:00Z",
  "source": "url" | "typed",
  "product": {"name": "Sentry", "url": "https://sentry.io"},
  "domain": "Developer Tools / Observability",
  "primary_user": "Software engineers & DevOps teams",
  "business_model": "B2B SaaS · Product-led growth",
  "core_problem": "Real-time application error tracking & code-level debugging",
  "current_focus": null | "launch" | "activation" | "retention" | "scaling" | "discovery",
  "confidence": "high" | "low"
}
```

Missing/optional fields are `null`, not guessed — later skills ask just-in-time for what they need. The typed path stays at 3 questions; `product.name` may be empty, `business_model`/`core_problem`/`current_focus` may be null, and the confirmation card renders only the lines we actually know.

## Code Layout (new)

```
cli/src/cli/onboard.py      # flow orchestration (prompt, fetch, confirm, save)
cli/src/cli/profile.py      # load/save baseline, `profile` + `setup` commands
cli/src/cli/infer.py        # heuristic domain/model inference from page text
cli/tests/test_onboard.py
cli/tests/test_infer.py
cli/tests/test_profile.py
```

- `paths` helper lives in `profile.py` for now (config dir resolution only: `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `~/.config`, Windows `%APPDATA%`), deliberately minimal to avoid coupling to the distribution plan.
- httpx used for fetch; inference has no network/LLM deps.

## Copy & Polish Rules (the Jobsian part)

- Total onboarding text on screen at once: one card, no scrolling paragraph.
- Voice: warm, direct, second person; no jargon dumps; no emoji.
- Every prompt has a sensible default or suggestion; Enter almost always works.
- Failure is silent-and-graceful: fetch errors fall to typed path without a scary traceback; one soft line (`Couldn't read that site — two quick questions instead.`).
- `--no-onboard` global flag to bypass (for scripting/tests); env `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_ONBOARD=1` equivalent.

## Constraints

- Python 3.10+, Typer, pytest — already in the workspace. `httpx` is **added** as a declared dependency of the `cli` package (builder check correction: it was not one; it is the fetch client of choice, and its `MockTransport` powers the fetch tests). Tests must not touch the real home dir (tmp_path + env overrides).
- Fetch tests use mocked transport (`httpx.MockTransport`), never live network.

## Review Focus (likely to bite)

1. Fetch hang/timeout on weird sites — hard 8s timeout, errors → typed path.
2. TTY detection wrong in some terminals — conservative check; hint-line behavior in non-TTY.
3. Inference confidently wrong — confirmation card always shown; nothing saved without confirm.
4. Concurrent first runs — file written atomically (temp file + replace).
5. `--version` and help must never trigger onboarding.

## Resolved Questions

1. Command naming: **`odi setup` / `odi profile`** (plain language; matches reserved `odi` alias). Copy uses the invoked program name.
2. `current_focus`: **just-in-time only** — not asked on the happy path; asked as the 3rd typed question in the fallback path.

## Builder Calls (made during review)

1. Typed-path fields: schema fields other than `schema_version` are nullable; card renders only non-null lines.
2. `httpx` added as an explicit `cli` package dependency (spec previously, incorrectly, claimed it already was).

Now I have everything to write both files. Let me settle the final decisions:

**Decisions (beyond user answers):**

1. **Semver/tag engine:** keep release-please from PR #8, but add `"skip-changelog": true` (no CHANGELOG.md committed) and `"draft": true` (draft GitHub Release = human publish gate that still honors "fully automated" — everything through generation+attachment is automatic; the only human act is clicking publish, which is the safety mechanism reconciling with "fully automated"). Wait — user said "fully automated AI rewrite at release time... with proper guardrails". They didn't say fully automated *publishing*... Actually my earlier design message said "draft the release for human approval before publishing" as a call, and the user's binding answer #1 says "fully automated AI rewrite at release time, with a disclaimer ... and guardrails". It doesn't explicitly authorize or forbid a publish gate. The task says: "draft-release human publish gate vs fully automated publish (user said fully automated — reconcile with a safety mechanism that still honors that)." So: keep automation end-to-end, but the safety mechanism = validation gates that fail closed + draft release + auto-publish on success? Hmm. Need a call that honors "fully automated" AND safety.

Reconcile: The workflow is fully automated: generate → validate (schema, SHA grounding, coverage, heuristic grounding) → if validation passes, attach changelog to release **and publish automatically**; if validation fails, the release is left as a **draft** (or the job fails and alerts maintainers) — that's the safety mechanism: fail-closed automation rather than a human gate on every release. So default path = zero human touch; humans only get involved when guardrails trip. That honors "fully automated" with a safety mechanism.

How to implement with release-please: release-please creates the release. With `"draft": true`, release is draft; our changelog workflow runs `on: release: published`? No — draft needs to be published. Alternative: release-please without draft creates a published release immediately; the changelog workflow on `release: created` then edits body + uploads changelog.json; on validation failure, job fails → release published but without proper changelog. Hmm, that's bad.

Better: release-please config `"draft": true` (releases created as drafts, already the case in PR #8? No — PR #8 has no draft option; default is published... actually release-please default creates non-draft releases? release-please creates releases as drafts when `draft: true`; default is false → published immediately on tag).

Design: set `"draft": true` in release-please-config.json. New workflow `changelog.yml` on `release: [created]` (fires for draft releases? `release: created` fires when release is created, including drafts — yes, GitHub `release` event `created` triggers for drafts created via API). It generates changelog from commits between previous tag and new tag, validates, uploads `changelog.json` + sets body, then **publishes the release** (`gh release edit --draft=false`) — fully automated. On validation failure: workflow fails, release stays draft → humans see a stuck draft. That's the safety mechanism: fail-closed.

But wait — release.yml (tag push) builds assets and uploads with softprops/action-gh-release; that works with draft releases too (it will edit the draft). Actually if release is draft and action-gh-release targets the tag, it finds the release and uploads. Fine. And e2e-install workflow may depend on release published? Let me not worry — note ordering.

Hmm, one issue: `release: created` for draft — GitHub docs: "created" fires when a release is published OR a draft is created? The event docs: `created` — "a release, pre-release, or draft of a release is created". Yes, drafts trigger `created`. Good.

Alternatively simpler: run changelog generation on tag push (`push: tags: v*`) and use `gh release` API to update body; release-please creates release (draft or not). To keep failure semantics, draft:true + publish-on-success is cleaner. I'll go: release-please `"draft": true`; changelog workflow on `release: types: [created]`; success → attach + publish; failure → stays draft (human intervention required, alarm). Fully automated normal path.

But does release-please support `draft` in config? Yes — release-please config supports `"draft": true` per package. I'm fairly confident (release-please manifest config supports `draft`... Actually I recall release-please config option "draft" exists for GitHub releases? There's `"skip-github-release"`... Let me think. release-please options include: `release-type`, `bump-minor-pre-major`, `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major`, `draft`, `prerelease`, `draft-pull-request`, `changelog-sections`, `skip-changelog`, `extra-files`... Yes, `draft` is a documented release-please config option (boolean, "Should this release be drafted?"). I'm reasonably confident. To be safe, the plan can have a fallback: if `draft` unsupported by the pinned action version, use `gh release edit` dance. I'll include verification step. Actually `skip-changelog` is also a release-please config option — yes ("skip-changelog: boolean, skip the changelog generation for this package"). Good.

2. **Backfill:** 0.1.0 initial release entry produced by the same generator running in "backfill mode": manifest built from full history `git log` root (since no tags), grouped, AI rewritten into a single "Initial release" section listing user-visible highlights, cited SHAs validated against the repo. Deterministic filtering + LLM. Produced at release time of v0.1.0 by the same workflow (range = all commits reachable from tag). No special case needed beyond "no previous tag → initial-release mode prompt variant".

3. **Grounding guardrails (concrete):**
   - Manifest: commit sha, subject, body, author, PR number, files changed, diffstat, type/scope parsed.
   - Prompt: only use manifest info; every entry cites ≥1 sha; sections fixed vocabulary: Added / Improved / Fixed / Security / Removed / Initial release; no technical jargon; value-focused.
   - Structured output: JSON schema (changelog.schema.json), `response_format`/schema-constrained decoding if provider supports; temperature 0; pinned model via env.
   - Validation (fail-closed): JSON schema validate; every cited sha ∈ manifest sha set (exact40-char or short? manifest uses full shas; model may abbreviate to 7 chars — accept sha prefix match ≥7 chars against manifest set); every entry has ≥1 source; each section name ∈ allowed set; coverage report: manifest commits with user-visible types (feat/fix/perf/refactor) must each be covered by ≥1 citation — else fail (or warn? complete list requirement → fail). Hidden types (ci/chore/test/docs/deps/build/refactor?) — wait, refactor: usually not user-visible but sometimes is. Define: hidden classes = ci, chore, test, docs, deps, build, style, revert(no)... "complete" honestly defined: complete over **user-visible changes** = feat, fix, perf + breaking refactors; internal classes (ci, chore, test, docs, deps, build, style, meta) excluded, and the generator must not claim coverage over them. Refactor → classified by prompt as hidden unless commit body indicates behavior change? That's non-deterministic. Better deterministic rule: manifest includes all commits; coverage requirement applies to types {feat, fix, perf} + any `!`/BREAKING; refactor/docs/etc are eligible-but-optional (the AI may include if value-bearing, but absence doesn't fail). Validation enforces: every feat/fix/perf/breaking commit is cited. That's "complete" honestly.
   - Hallucination heuristic: extract identifiers/proper nouns from generated text (tokens with CamelCase/`code formatting`/UPPER_SNAKE/version numbers) and require each appears in manifest text; unknown ones → fail. Keep conservative (only check "risky" tokens: backticked code, camelCase, snake_case, ALLCAPS, semver-looking, file paths) to avoid false positives on prose words.
   - Anti-fabrication: also validate no sha of *any* git object outside range? Simpler: sha must be in range manifest — done.
   - Self-check pass: second deterministic validator function (no second LLM call needed).
   - Provider: OpenAI-compatible chat completions via env `AGENTIC_ODI_CHANGELOG_BASE_URL/…_MODEL/…_API_KEY`; offline mode `--fixture` / `CHANGELOG_FIXTURE_DIR` for tests: harness injects a fake client.

4. **Runtime surface:**
   - `odi whats-new [--since VERSION] [--all] [--json]` with `changelog` as alias? Keep one command: `odi changelog` primary? Earlier I suggested `odi whats-new` / `odi changelog`. Pick primary `odi changelog` (matches user's word) with `--since`, `--all`, `--json`. And auto-show: on first run after an update? MVP: no auto-prompt; maybe print nothing automatically. Keep minimal: command only. Actually a nice touch: after successful `odi update`, print "Run 'odi changelog' to see what's new." — one line in update_cmd. Cheap, include it.
   - Last-run tracking: `update.json` state file (paths.state_file()) currently `{"last_check": …}` written by `record_check` which **overwrites** the whole file — must be changed to merge keys (that's a modification to update.py — note!). Add `last_run_version`: recorded in root callback after startup (only when frozen? no — record always, path may be unwritable when not frozen; guard). Store `{"last_check": …, "last_run_version": "0.1.0"}`. `record_check` must read-merge-write to not clobber `last_run_version`. Mark this edit BLOCKED on PR #8.
   - Fetch: `GET https://api.github.com/repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases` (list) — for each release in range, download `changelog.json` asset via browser_download_url (asset URL pattern like existing `_RELEASES_DOWNLOAD`). Range: versions between `since` (state last_run_version, or `--since`) and current `__version__`. Compose oldest→newest. Skip drafts/prereleases. Offline/4xx → one soft line. Note: `update.py` has `RELEASES_API` latest-only; new module `cli/src/cli/changelog.py` fetches releases list.
   - Where code lives: pure model/render/compare in `core/src/core/changelog.py` (pydantic — core has pydantic); fetch+compose in `cli/src/cli/changelog.py` (urllib, like update.py). Hmm — GUI later wants same fetch; but GUI (Streamlit) could reuse `core` too... Fetch in core vs cli? update.py already does urllib fetch in cli. Put fetch in cli for now; core holds schema + render + range logic (GUI can call cli module? no — client doesn't depend on cli). Alternative: put everything in `core/changelog.py` including fetch (stdlib only) so both CLI and client reuse. Core is "domain models" but adding a small fetch function is pragmatic. I'll decide: **schema + parsing + range + rendering in `core`**; **fetch in core too** (`core/changelog.py`, stdlib urllib, injected `fetch` callable for tests) so GUI reuses; CLI command is a thin Typer wrapper. Core already pure-pydantic; adding urllib-based fetch is fine and keeps one implementation. Mark as builder call.
   - Actually check core deps: pydantic only, no httpx. stdlib urllib consistent with update.py. OK.

5. **Filtering / "complete" definition:** as above. Also hide `refactor`? Include in hidden classes: `chore`, `ci`, `build`, `test`, `docs`, `style`, `deps` (as scope of chore), and `refactor` by default (may be surfaced by AI if it delivers user value — but coverage requirement doesn't apply). Hmm wait: refactor often user-visible-ish (performance/UX unchanged semantics). Keep rule: coverage-required types = {feat, fix, perf, breaking}; coverage-excluded = {chore, ci, build, test, docs, style, refactor}; `revert` → coverage-required (a revert undoes a user-visible change → treat like fix). Good, deterministic.

6. **Commit/branch enforcement tooling decision:** commitizen (`cz`) — add as dev dependency? Workspace root has no dev-deps group? Root pyproject `package = false`. Dev deps might be per-package. pre-commit hook can use `commitizen` via local repo + language: system/python. Simplest robust: add a `local` pre-commit hook running `uv run cz check --rev-range`? commit-msg hook via pre-commit: pre-commit supports `commit-msg` stage hooks; use `commitizen`'s `cz check --message`? Not directly a pre-commit hook... commitizen provides `commitizen` pre-commit hook? They have hooks: `commitizen-branch`, `commitizen-commit`... Hmm. Simpler alternative: use `conventional-pre-commit` (parkerbryce/conventional-pre-commit) — a purpose-built pre-commit hook validating Conventional Commits messages. Very low risk. But also want `cz commit` scaffolding — optional; skip scaffolding to reduce scope, just validation. CI: PR title check via `commitizen` too heavy; write a tiny Python script `scripts/check_pr_title.py` (regex for conventional PR title, allow `deps`/`Release` etc.?) — dependabot titles `chore(deps): bump ...` pass conventional regex. Branch name check: tiny `scripts/check_branch_name.py` or pure bash regex job. To keep consistent: implement both as `scripts/ci/check_conventional.py` (mode: title|branch). Actually keep plan crisp: one script `scripts/check_commit_convention.py` with subcommands. Hmm, simpler: two small scripts or one script with two functions + `python -m`. I'll spec: `scripts/check_convention.py` handling `pr-title` and `branch-name` modes, unit-tested? Tests for scripts — maybe skip unit tests, CI job itself is the test (validate in test step with sample strings? include self-test mode). Keep: add pytest test file `scripts/tests/test_check_convention.py`? scripts isn't a package... Tests could live in `cli/tests`? No. Put script logic importable and test from a root `tests/`? There's no root tests dir. Option: make convention checker a module in `core` (`core/src/core/convention.py`) with pure functions (conventional_title regex, branch name regex) + tests in core/tests, and CI script is a 5-line wrapper `python -c` calling it, or a console entry. That's clean: logic tested in core, CI job: `uv run --directory core python -m core.convention pr-title "$PR_TITLE"`? module main. Or `python -c "from core.convention import ..."`. I'll spec core module `convention.py` with `main()` guard. Good — testable, no new deps.

Also `BREAKING CHANGE`/scopes list lives there (shared with manifest builder? manifest builder is in scripts). Reuse `core.convention` from scripts too.

7. **Tag/release counting:** first release 0.1.0 already in manifest (`".": "0.1.0"`). Interesting — PR #8's manifest says 0.1.0 but no tags exist yet. So release-please's first Release PR will bump to 0.1.1? Since manifest already claims 0.1.0 with no tag... release-please creates release PR from commits since... first run with no tags: it will propose 0.1.0 release (manifest0.1.0 but no release exists → it may still open release-please-manifest initial release of 0.1.0? release-please uses tags; if v0.1.0 tag missing, it creates PR to release 0.1.0). Fine — first release will be 0.1.0 per facts given. Backfill mode handles no-previous-tag.

8. **AI provider in CI:** needs an API key in repo secrets (OPENAI_API_KEY or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Note as ops prerequisite. Model pinned via env `CHANGELOG_MODEL`. Fallback: if secret absent → generation fails → release stays draft (fail-closed) — but that blocks releases for contributors without secret. Note: maintainer-only repo, acceptable; document.

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "date": "2026-10-18",

Also a per-entry optional `breaking: bool`.

Release body: rendered markdown from changelog.json (same renderer used by CLI) + disclaimer footer. Generated at release time: body = markdown render of the JSON. **Version range logic:** since < current, ordered by semver; include all releases with since < v <= current. Versions not valid semver → skip with note. Releases without changelog.json asset → note "not available for vX" (only affects earliest pre-feature releases).

**last_run_version update:** when? Record `last_run_version = __version__` at every successful command run (root callback), so next run's `--since` = that version. But then `odi changelog` invoked explicitly: it should show since last *shown*? Design: `last_run_version` records last version seen/reported. On `odi changelog`, show since `last_run_version`, then update it to current. On ordinary runs, update silently (so if user never opens changelog, first `odi changelog` after N updates shows... hmm, if ordinary runs update the marker, then `odi changelog` would show nothing new because marker tracks latest run not last *seen* changelog). I'll document this reconciliation explicitly in the design: marker = last version whose changelog was displayed; initialized to current on first run (fresh install shows current release's notes? MVP: initialize marker to current version → first `odi changelog` with no marker shows *all* releases available (since there's no baseline) — actually better: if marker missing → show all published releases (complete history), then set marker. Confirmed: `uv run --directory core` chdirs to core. So generator tests can run as `uv run --directory core pytest ../scripts/changelog/tests -v` from repo root (cwd becomes core, path ../scripts/... resolves). And generator script run: `uv run --directory core python ../scripts/changelog/generate.py` (script dir → sys.path[0]=scripts/changelog; `import core` works since core installed in that env).

Wait — but if bandit doesn't scan scripts and mypy doesn't either, and ruff does scan (workspace-wide `ruff check .` with root config discovery). Root pyproject has no [tool.ruff] — defaults apply (88 cols, E4,E7,E9,F,I? no — default select is ["E4","E7","E9","F"]; isort (I) not default). To match house style (100 cols), add `[tool.ruff]` + `[tool.ruff.lint]` to root pyproject. Hmm but careful: root pyproject changes could affect ruff's handling of package dirs? Each package pyproject overrides anyway (nearest config wins). Files directly under scripts/ and root would use root config. Safe. I'll include it as a small step (and re-run `uv run ruff check .` + `ruff format --check .`).

Wait — one more: does root pyproject already have [tool.bandit]? `-c pyproject.toml` — presumably yes with skips. Not relevant.

Also decide: does `test` job get a new step for generator tests, or fold into "Pytest (core)"? New step after Pytest (core): 
```yaml
- name: Pytest (changelog generator)
  run: uv run --directory core pytest ../scripts/changelog/tests -v
```
No coverage merge impact. Also `ci-green` needs `test` — unchanged since we're adding a step within existing job. But Task 1 adds a NEW CI job (convention checks) → must add to `ci-green.needs`.

Convention job: `pr-title` check needs `pull_request` event title; branch name needs `github.head_ref`. Job:
```yaml
  convention:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    ...run: uv run --directory core python -m core.convention pr-title "$PR_TITLE" and branch "$HEAD_REF"
```
Hmm module main: `python -m core.convention` with args. Or a small script. I'll spec `core/src/core/convention.py` with functions + `main(argv)` and `if __name__ == "__main__"`. Called as `uv run --directory core python -m core.convention pr-title --title "$TITLE"`.

Wait: does main() run only for PRs? Job conditioned `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` — but then ci-green.needs includes `convention`, and on push events convention job is skipped → `needs.*.result` = "skipped" → ci-green fails ("skipped" != "success")! Check ci-green logic: `if [ "$result" != "success" ]` → fail on skipped. And ci-green `if: always()`. So a skipped convention job would fail ci-green on pushes to main. Options: convention job runs on both push and PR (on push, validate last commit message(s) instead of PR title — even better: push → check commit messages of head commit; PR → check title + head branch). Then never skipped. 

I'll spec: `convention` job always runs; step script uses `github.event_name`: pull_request → PR title + head_ref branch; push → head commit subject + branch name (github.ref_name; main allowed by allowlist). Good.

Now, do we enforce scope enums strictly? Dependent PR titles from dependabot `chore(deps): bump ...` OK. Keep allowed types list + optional scope (any word). Branch allowlist: `main`, `dependabot/**`, `renovate/**` exempt.

Enforcement local: pre-commit commit-msg hook. Use `conventional-pre-commit`? That pulls a remote repo hook. Alternatively a local hook: `repo: local, hooks: [id: conventional-commit, entry: bash -c 'uv run --directory core python -m core.convention commit-message' ...]` — pre-commit passes filename... commit-msg hooks receive the commit message file path as arg. local hook: `entry: uv run python -m core.convention commit-message-file`, `language: system`, `stages: [commit-msg]`. But `uv run` inside pre-commit from root... entry runs from repo root: `uv run --directory core python -m core.convention commit-msg-file` — wait pre-commit's language: system runs entry directly. cwd = repo root (pre-commit runs hooks from repo root? hooks run in cwd of repo). Should work. Simpler & robust: `language: python` local hook with additional_dependencies? local python hook installs the repo dir as package — root isn't a package. Use `language: system` + entry `uv run --directory core python -m core.convention commit-msg-file "$1"`... pre-commit appends the filename args. Entry: `uv run --directory core python -m core.convention commit-msg-file` and pre-commit passes the msg file path as final positional arg → main accepts it. Wait but does pre-commit allow `stages: [commit-msg]`? Modern pre-commit: stages named `commit-msg`. Yes (pre-commit >= 3 uses `commit-msg` stage name... older used `commit-msg` too). Root pre-commit config exists with ruff hooks (stages default pre-commit). Add:

```yaml
- repo: local
  hooks:
    - id: conventional-commit-message
      name: conventional commit message
      entry: uv run --directory core python -m core.convention commit-msg-file
      language: system
      stages: [commit-msg]
      pass_filenames: true
```

Good enough; TDD step includes testing via pytest (message validity function) rather than actually running pre-commit in CI (pre-commit not in CI? CI doesn't run pre-commit — ruff run directly). Fine.

Also document branch standard + squash-merge policy in docs; branch-name enforcement only via CI (git doesn't intercept branch creation easily) — could add pre-push hook but skip (anti-goal: heavy tooling). Document recommended PR merge method = squash (GitHub branch protection setting — repo settings, manual step; list as ops prerequisite, not code).

Where do docs live? No CONTRIBUTING.md exists. Create `docs/development/standards.md`? Or CONTRIBUTING.md — GitHub surfaces CONTRIBUTING.md automatically on PR creation — best practice: create `CONTRIBUTING.md` at root with commit/branch/PR standard + pointer. I'll create CONTRIBUTING.md (single file, discoverable). README link optional (README is huge; add one line under development section? Keep: add pointer line — but README edits risk conflicts... minor. I'll include README pointer as optional in Task 7... user said don't touch other files — that's about ME now, not the plan).

Now the deliverables. Let me also double check release-please `skip-changelog` + `draft` options... I can't network? I do have web tools. Quick check via webfetch of release-please README config docs would strengthen grounding. Let me do a quick search/fetch.
Try the repo docs path or the website: release-please docs at https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/configuration.md might be in docs/ folder... Or search.

Confirmed release-please options: `skip-changelog`, `draft`, **`force-tag-creation`** (important with draft: without it, draft releases don't create tags until publish → release-please can't find previous release → wrong changelog ranges AND our generator's tag-based range would break!). Critical: set `force-tag-creation: true` alongside `draft: true`.

But wait — if tag is created immediately while release is draft, then `release.yml` (trigger: push tags v*) fires immediately... Tags created by release-please via API — does that trigger `push` tag workflows? Tags created through the GitHub API (git data API) do trigger workflows? Tags created via API using GITHUB_TOKEN... Events created by GITHUB_TOKEN don't trigger other workflows (the GitHub recursion prevention). release-please uses GITHUB_TOKEN → tag push event from GITHUB_TOKEN won't trigger release.yml! Hmm — but this is already the case with PR #8's design (release-please tags with its token; release.yml on tag push). Known issue: release-please-action docs address this — actually release-please creates tags via the API, and `push` events for tags created via API *do* fire workflow `push` events? GitHub docs: "events triggered by the GITHUB_TOKEN will not create a new workflow run" — this applies to events *using* GITHUB_TOKEN as the actor. Tags created via API with GITHUB_TOKEN do NOT trigger workflows. BUT release-please-action docs commonly show release workflows on `release: published` or on tag push... Many projects use `on: push: tags` with release-please successfully? Hmm. Actually the recursion prevention: an event *caused by* GITHUB_TOKEN won't trigger. Tags pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN won't trigger `push` workflows. So how do release-please projects run build-on-tag? They typically trigger on `release: published` instead... or they use a PAT. 

Wait — but release-please itself creates the GitHub Release; release event `created`/`published` by GITHUB_TOKEN also won't trigger workflows. This is a real chicken-and-egg. release-please-action README: they suggest workflows on `release: types: [published]`... which also suffers? Hmm.

Actually the docs say: "When you use the repository's GITHUB_TOKEN to perform tasks, events triggered by the GITHUB_TOKEN, with the exception of workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch, will not create a new workflow run." So release-please's tag/release creation won't trigger our changelog workflow or release.yml.

But PR #8's design already relies on release.yml triggered by tag push... which apparently may not fire. This is a pre-existing concern of PR #8 (not mine to fix necessarily, but my changelog workflow inherits it). Hmm, wait — is it true that API-created tags don't fire push events? The recursion guard applies to *events* (workflow runs) caused by GITHUB_TOKEN. Tags created via API → push event has actor = GITHUB_TOKEN user → suppressed. Yes, widely documented that release-please + `on: push: tags` doesn't work and you should use `on: release` with... also suppressed? Also commonly people DO use `release: types: [published]` with release-please and it works? Let me not go down this hole — but it materially affects my design.Actually, many real projects do: release-please creates release PR; on merge to main, release-please creates tag + release; a separate workflow `on: release: published` builds assets. And these work — because... hmm, do they? There are numerous issues "release-please does not trigger workflows on release created". The standard answer from release-please wiki: "workflows triggered by release events won't run because GITHUB_TOKEN" → recommend using `push` to main after release PR merge as trigger, or use a PAT/GitHub App token.

But note PR #8's release.yml `on: push: tags: v*`. When release-please merges its release PR (merged by a *human* → the merge commit push is a human actor), then release-please-action runs on that push event (workflow release-please.yml triggered by human push — allowed) and creates the tag+release with GITHUB_TOKEN → tag push event suppressed → release.yml never runs?? Hmm, that would break PR #8's build pipeline... unless tag creation via API still fires.I should not fully resolve GitHub's event matrix from memory. My design's robust option: **trigger the changelog job from within the release-please workflow itself?** No — release-please job runs before tag exists... Actually release-please creates tag+release in the same job step. A follow-up step in release-please.yml after the action step could run the generation using the action's outputs (`outputs.tag_name`, `outputs.paths_changed`, `outputs.releases_created`). release-please-action v4 exposes `tag_name` and `releases_created` outputs! So: add steps to release-please.yml after the action: if `releases_created == 'true'` → checkout with fetch-depth 0 → generate → validate → upload asset + set body + publish draft. Single workflow, no event-matrix uncertainty, ordering guaranteed (same job, after release creation). Tag exists at that point (force-tag-creation). 

And release.yml (assets) trigger: that's PR #8's concern (tag push may or may not fire — their problem/design already approved; actually if suppressed, PR #8's assets never build... but not mine to fix; though I could note it as a risk/open question in the design "Review Focus" — flagging: if tag-push events are suppressed for GITHUB_TOKEN-created tags, release.yml must instead trigger on `release: published` or be chained; out of scope but noted). Hmm — actually wait: if release.yml never fires, my changelog publish step order vs assets... The changelog job publishes the draft → if release.yml triggered on `release: published`... PR8 has tag push. I'll note this as a cross-plan risk with recommendation, but keep my implementation chained into release-please.yml (robust regardless).

Actually hold on — simpler and even more robust: chain changelog generation into `release-please.yml` as a follow-up job in the SAME workflow (`needs: release-please`, conditioned on `steps.rp.outputs.releases_created == 'true'`). Job-level needs with outputs. Then generate from the tag, edit release body (via gh CLI), upload asset, `gh release edit --draft=false`. Fully automated; fail-closed (job fails → release stays draft).

But there's a subtlety: does the release-please action step need `id:` and outputs — yes, `id: release-please`, outputs: `releases_created`, `tag_name`, `paths_changed`. v4 supports these outputs. 

Draft + force-tag-creation: with force-tag-creation the tag exists → but tag push still happens via API (suppressed for workflows, fine). Our job uses `fetch-depth: 0` checkout and computes range by tags: previous tag = tag before new tag. Generator: `git tag --list 'v*' --sort=v:refname`, find previous; if none → backfill mode (whole history).

Also release.yml triggered by tag push: with force-tag-creation the tag push event by GITHUB_TOKEN → likely suppressed → PR8 assets build issue. Note as risk + recommended fix (chain asset build after changelog job or trigger release.yml on `workflow_dispatch`/repository_dispatch or PAT). Out of my scope but MUST flag in design's Review Focus since my design interacts (ordering: publish draft before/after assets?). Ordering target: generate+validate+attach changelog → publish draft → assets build → e2e install. If asset build is chained too (recommend PR #8 amend: move build into release-please workflow chain), perfect ordering. I'll flag: "Cross-plan recommendation: PR #8 should chain its build matrix after release creation (same workflow) rather than relying on tag-push events, because tag pushes created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger workflows; this also gives deterministic ordering with the changelog job."

Hmm, is that true though? Let me verify quickly — this is a load-bearing claim. Search.
